One day · East to West End · Mostly free

Glasgow in a day — all your stops on one map

Start with old Glasgow in the morning — Cathedral, Necropolis, then back through the centre to GoMA. In between, the Old Town architecture walk (dotted line on the map) links George Square and the Merchant City up High Street to the Cathedral — a walk, not another stop. Spend the afternoon in the West End at the University cloisters and the Botanic Gardens. Glasgow Central and Queen Street stations are marked for reference — both are a short walk from GoMA (3).

4–5

Afternoon — West EndUniversity of Glasgow → Botanic Gardens. Head west via Byres Road, lunch on Ashton Lane.

Your location — blue dotAppears when you tap “Show my location” above and allow location access, then keeps updating live as you move until you tap “Stop tracking”. Only the dot moves — and the pale circle around it, which is how accurate the fix is; the map itself stays exactly where it is.

Numbers are visit order, not distance order on the map: east (1–2) → centre (3) → West End (4–5). The dotted walk covers the old town between the centre and the Cathedral, and the star murals sit along the way — St Mungo is right on the walk's High Street leg.

Morning — Old Glasgow

1

Glasgow Cathedral

Castle St, Glasgow G4 0QZ

12th-century cathedral — the only mainland Scottish medieval cathedral to survive the Reformation almost intact. Don't miss St Mungo's tomb in the Lower Church.

FreeMon–Sat 10am–4pmSun 1–4pm★ 4.5
DirectionsOpen in Maps
2

Glasgow Necropolis

Castle St, Glasgow — directly behind the Cathedral

Victorian garden cemetery on the hill behind the Cathedral — around 3,500 monuments, the John Knox monument, and the best view back over the cathedral and city. Cross the bridge from stop 1, it's 2 minutes away.

FreeDaily 7am–4:30pm★ 4.6
DirectionsOpen in Maps
3

Gallery of Modern Art — GoMA

111 Queen St, Royal Exchange Square, Glasgow G1 3AH

Contemporary art in a grand neoclassical building in Royal Exchange Square. The Duke of Wellington statue outside is invariably wearing a traffic cone — that's your photo stop on the walk down through Merchant City and George Square.

FreeMon–Thu & Sat 10am–5pmFri & Sun 11am–5pm★ 4.4
DirectionsOpen in Maps

Afternoon — West End

4

University of Glasgow

University Ave, Glasgow G12 8QQ

Head west to the Gothic main building and its cloisters — the vaulted undercroft is the bit everyone photographs. Wander up through Kelvingrove Park on the way; it's a short hop from here to the Botanics.

Free to wanderGrounds & cloisters — daytime★ 4.6
DirectionsOpen in Maps
5

Glasgow Botanic Gardens

730 Great Western Rd, Glasgow G12 0UE

Victorian glasshouses on the River Kelvin — the Kibble Palace, a huge wrought-iron glasshouse of tree ferns, is the highlight. Calm end to the day; Ashton Lane / Byres Road nearby for food afterwards.

FreeGardens daily 7am–6pm★ 4.5
DirectionsOpen in Maps

Old Town architecture walk — not a stop

Merchant City · High Street · George Square walk

About 45–60 minutes at a looking-up pace · George Square → Cathedral

The dotted line on the map — it follows the streets, not a straight line: east on George Street, down Montrose Street and Ingram Street through Merchant City to Albion Street, across Trongate, then up High Street and Castle Street to the Cathedral. Do it between GoMA (3) and the Cathedral (1), in either direction — it's the architecture of the old town, walked rather than visited.

  • George Square & City ChambersThe square's statues and the City Chambers (1888) — Glasgow's Victorian showpiece, all marble and mosaics inside the grand entrance hall.

  • Merchant City — Merchant Square, Albion StGrand 18th–19th-century warehouses and merchants' houses around Ingram St and Bell St, built on tobacco and sugar money.

  • Tolbooth Steeple, foot of High StreetThe 1626 steeple is all that survives of the old Tolbooth at Glasgow Cross — the historic heart of the city.

  • High Street up to Provand's LordshipGlasgow's oldest street, climbing to Provand's Lordship (1471) — the city's oldest house — opposite the Cathedral, where the walk ends.

Street art — spot them as you pass

City Centre Mural Trail highlights

Star pins on the map — not itinerary stops, just worth looking up for as the day takes you past them.

  • ★

    St Mungo mural — 287 High StreetSmug's huge portrait of Glasgow's patron saint, modern dress, robin on his hand. Right on the architecture walk's High Street leg.

  • ★

    Fellow Glasgow Residents — Ingram StreetSmug again: the wildlife of Glasgow — foxes, deer, squirrels — across a Merchant City car-park wall.

  • ★

    Billy Connolly: “75 BC” — Mitchell StreetJohn Byrne's portrait for Connolly's 75th birthday, windblown coat and all, just off Buchanan Street.

  • ★

    Billy Connolly: “Big Banana Feet” — Dixon StreetRachel Maclean's take on the Big Yin in his banana boots, near St Enoch Square.

  • ★

    Billy Connolly: “Dr Connolly, I Presume?” — Kent StreetJack Vettriano's Connolly in a windswept landscape, by the Barrowland in the east end — the third of the 75th-birthday murals.

About Google My Maps — the honest answer

You asked if I could just do it in My Maps. I can't create one inside your Google account from here — a My Map lives in your Google Drive and needs you signed in, and Google only lets you create/edit on desktop (phones can view).

That's why this page exists: it gives you the same thing right now — all stops on one map, numbered pins, colour groups and a legend — with no account and no desktop needed. For turn-by-turn navigation on the day, use the “Open full route in Google Maps” button at the top — it loads stops 1–5 in order in the normal Maps app.

If you still want your own My Map as well, the steps on the right take about 5 minutes on a computer and use exactly the names/addresses on this page.

Make it in My Maps yourself (optional)

  1. On a computer, go to google.com/mymaps → Create a new map.
  2. Search and add each stop in order: Glasgow Cathedral, Glasgow Necropolis, Gallery of Modern Art, University of Glasgow, Glasgow Botanic Gardens.
  3. Add a second layer for reference: Glasgow Central and Glasgow Queen Street stations, plus the mural spots if you want them — layers are My Maps' closest thing to a legend.
  4. Colour layer 1's pins for morning/afternoon. Use numbered markers if you want the same 1–5 order as here.
  5. Title it, then Share — on your phone, open it via Google Maps → Saved → Maps.

Caveat worth knowing: My Maps has no proper on-map legend panel — the layer list is the legend. This page's legend above is clearer for just looking at the day.

Hours and ratings checked at build time — check on the day for special closures. The stops listed are free to enter or wander.
